tool_response.originalFile:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe skogai command runner: typed io for handing work to agents
#
# every agent call is `prompt + files -> json matching a schema`.
# pure by default: only `--apply` changes existing files, scaffolds only create new ones.
# @meta require-tools jq,yq,git,claude
# @meta dotenv
# @meta binname argc
# @env SKOGAI_MODEL=sonnet                         default model for agent calls
# @env ARGC_DOCS=~/.local/src/argc/docs           argc docs handed to `improve`
# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$PWD"
PLUGINS="$ROOT/plugins"
SCHEMAS="$PLUGINS/skogai-runner/schemas"
WORKORDERS="$ROOT/.skogai/workorders"
LOGS="$ROOT/.skogai/logs/argc"

# @cmd send a prompt and files to an agent, print its typed output
#
# the prompt comes from --prompt or stdin. files are inlined as
# <file path="..."> blocks, so the agent needs no tools to read them.
# with --schema stdout is the json object, without it plain text.
# @option -p --prompt                  prompt text, read from stdin if omitted
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            file to inline
# @option -s --schema[?`_choice_schema`] schema name or path for the output
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to $SKOGAI_MODEL
# @option -t --tools                   tools the agent may use, none if omitted
# @option -a --allow*                  allowed tool patterns, e.g. "Bash(git log *)"
# @option    --plugin-dir* <DIR>       plugin to load into the agent
# @flag      --raw                     print the full result envelope
# @alias s
send() {
    local prompt="${argc_prompt:-$(cat)}"
    _compose "$prompt" "${argc_file[@]}" |
        _agent "${argc_schema:-}" "${argc_model:-$SKOGAI_MODEL}" "${argc_tools:-}" "${argc_raw:-}"
}

# @cmd ask an agent to edit files, print the patch. pure unless --apply
#
# the agent returns whole files (schema `edit`), the patch is derived
# here with `git diff`, so a bad hunk header can never break it.
# @arg request~                        what to change
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            files to hand over, default Argcfile.sh and the runner skill
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to $SKOGAI_MODEL
# @flag      --apply                   apply the patch to the tree
# @alias i
improve() {
    local files=("${argc_file[@]}")
    [[ ${#files[@]} -gt 0 ]] || files=(Argcfile.sh plugins/skogai-runner/skills/argc/SKILL.md)
    local docs="${ARGC_DOCS/#\~/$HOME}"
    local ctx=()
    [[ -f "$docs/specification.md" ]] && ctx+=("$docs/specification.md")
    [[ -f "$docs/command-runner.md" ]] && ctx+=("$docs/command-runner.md")

    local prompt
    prompt="$(printf '%s\n\n%s\n%s\n' "${argc_request[*]}" \
        "return every file you change in full, paths relative to the repo root." \
        "only these files may change: ${files[*]}")"

    local out patch
    out="$(_compose "$prompt" "${files[@]}" "${ctx[@]}" | _agent edit "${argc_model:-$SKOGAI_MODEL}" "" "")"
    patch="$(_edit_to_patch "$out" "${files[@]}")"
    jq -r '.summary' <<<"$out" >&2
    if [[ -z "$patch" ]]; then
        echo "empty patch" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "${argc_apply:-}" ]]; then
        git apply --check <<<"$patch"
        git apply <<<"$patch"
        git diff --stat -- "${files[@]}" >&2
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$patch"
        return 1
    fi
}

# @cmd workorders: one bounded question, gathered inputs, checkable output
wo() { :; }

# @cmd scaffold a workorder
# @arg name!                           kebab-case name
# @option -s --schema[?`_choice_schema`] output schema, default answer
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            input files
# @option -t --tools                   tools the worker may use
wo::new() {
    local path="$WORKORDERS/$argc_name.md"
    [[ ! -e "$path" ]] || { echo "exists: $path" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$WORKORDERS"
    {
        echo "---"
        echo "type: workorder"
        echo "title: $argc_name"
        echo "schema: ${argc_schema:-answer}"
        echo "tools: \"${argc_tools:-}\""
        echo "files:"
        local f
        for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do echo "  - $f"; done
        echo "---"
        echo
        echo "<one bounded question>"
    } >"$path"
    echo "$path"
}

# @cmd run a workorder, write <name>.result.json beside it
# @arg workorder![`_choice_workorder`] name or path
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to the workorder's or $SKOGAI_MODEL
wo::run() {
    local path
    path="$(_workorder_path "$argc_workorder")"
    local fm
    fm="$(yq --front-matter=extract -o json '.' "$path")"
    [[ "$(jq -r '.type' <<<"$fm")" == workorder ]] || { echo "not a workorder: $path" >&2; return 2; }

    local files=() f
    while IFS= read -r f; do [[ -n "$f" ]] && files+=("$f"); done < <(jq -r '.files // [] | .[]' <<<"$fm")
    local schema model tools
    schema="$(jq -r '.schema // "answer"' <<<"$fm")"
    model="${argc_model:-$(jq -r --arg d "$SKOGAI_MODEL" '.model // $d' <<<"$fm")}"
    tools="$(jq -r '.tools // ""' <<<"$fm")"

    local result="${path%.md}.result.json"
    _compose "$(_body "$path")" "${files[@]}" | _agent "$schema" "$model" "$tools" "" >"$result"
    cat "$result"
}

# @cmd list workorders and whether they have a result
wo::ls() {
    local f
    for f in "$WORKORDERS"/*.md; do
        [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
        if [[ -e "${f%.md}.result.json" ]]; then echo "done  $(basename "$f" .md)"; else echo "open  $(basename "$f" .md)"; fi
    done
}

# @cmd claude code plugins under plugins/
plugin() { :; }

# @cmd scaffold a plugin with one skill
# @arg name!                           kebab-case name
# @arg description!                    one line: what it is for
plugin::new() {
    local dir="$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
    [[ ! -e "$dir" ]] || { echo "exists: $dir" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude-plugin" "$dir/skills/$argc_name"
    jq -n --arg n "$argc_name" --arg d "$argc_description" \
        '{name: $n, version: "0.1.0", description: $d, author: {name: "skogix"}}' >"$dir/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
    printf -- '---\nname: %s\ndescription: %s\n---\n\n# %s\n' \
        "$argc_name" "$argc_description" "$argc_name" >"$dir/skills/$argc_name/SKILL.md"
    echo "$dir"
}

# @cmd validate plugins, all if no name is given
# @arg name*[`_choice_plugin`]
plugin::check() {
    local names=("${argc_name[@]}") n
    [[ ${#names[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t names < <(_choice_plugin)
    for n in "${names[@]}"; do claude plugin validate "$PLUGINS/$n"; done
}

# @cmd run a plugin's evals
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]
plugin::eval() {
    claude plugin eval "$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
}

# @cmd hand a plugin to an agent for improvement, pure unless --apply
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]
# @arg request~                        what to change
# @flag --apply                        apply the patch to the tree
plugin::improve() {
    local files=()
    mapfile -t files < <(git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard "plugins/$argc_name")
    argc_file=("${files[@]}")
    improve
}

# @cmd static checks on the runner itself: argc parse, shellcheck, schemas, plugins
check() {
    argc --argc-export Argcfile.sh >/dev/null && echo "ok    argc parse"
    if command -v shellcheck >/dev/null; then
        shellcheck -x Argcfile.sh && echo "ok    shellcheck"
    else
        echo "skip  shellcheck: not installed"
    fi
    local s
    for s in "$SCHEMAS"/*.json; do jq -e . "$s" >/dev/null && echo "ok    schema $(basename "$s")"; done
    plugin::check
}

# prompt + files -> one message
_compose() {
    local prompt="$1"
    shift
    printf '<prompt>\n%s\n</prompt>\n' "$prompt"
    local f
    for f in "$@"; do
        [[ -f "$f" ]] || { echo "no such file: $f" >&2; return 2; }
        printf '\n<file path="%s">\n%s\n</file>\n' "$f" "$(cat "$f")"
    done
}

# message on stdin -> typed output on stdout, envelope logged
# _agent <schema> <model> <tools> <raw>
_agent() {
    local schema="$1" model="$2" tools="$3" raw="$4"
    local args=(-p --output-format json --model "$model" --tools "$tools" --permission-mode dontAsk)
    local a
    for a in "${argc_allow[@]}"; do args+=(--allowedTools "$a"); done
    for a in "${argc_plugin_dir[@]}"; do args+=(--plugin-dir "$a"); done
    [[ -n "$schema" ]] && args+=(--json-schema "$(jq -c . "$(_schema_path "$schema")")")

    mkdir -p "$LOGS"
    local log
    log="$LOGS/$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)-$$.json"
    claude "${args[@]}" >"$log"

    if [[ -n "$raw" ]]; then cat "$log"; fi
    if [[ "$(jq -r '.is_error' "$log")" == true ]]; then
        jq -r '.result // .subtype' "$log" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    [[ -n "$raw" ]] && return 0
    if [[ -n "$schema" ]]; then jq '.structured_output' "$log"; else jq -r '.result' "$log"; fi
}

# edit json + allowed files -> unified diff, refusing paths outside the list
_edit_to_patch() {
    local out="$1"
    shift
    local new path allowed f
    new="$(mktemp)"
    trap 'rm -f "$new"' RETURN
    while IFS= read -r path; do
        allowed=
        for f in "$@"; do [[ "$path" == "$f" ]] && allowed=1; done
        [[ -n "$allowed" ]] || { echo "refused: $path is not a handed-over file" >&2; return 2; }
        jq -j --arg p "$path" '.files[] | select(.path == $p) | .content' <<<"$out" >"$new"
        diff -u --label "a/$path" --label "b/$path" "$path" "$new" || true
    done < <(jq -r '.files[].path' <<<"$out")
}

_body() { awk 'NR==1 && /^---$/ {fm=1; next} fm && /^---$/ {fm=0; next} !fm' "$1"; }

_schema_path() {
    if [[ -f "$1" ]]; then echo "$1"; else echo "$SCHEMAS/$1.json"; fi
}

_workorder_path() {
    if [[ -f "$1" ]]; then echo "$1"; else echo "$WORKORDERS/$1.md"; fi
}

_choice_schema() {
    local f
    for f in "$SCHEMAS"/*.json; do basename "$f" .json; done
}

_choice_workorder() {
    local f
    for f in "$WORKORDERS"/*.md; do [[ -e "$f" ]] && basename "$f" .md; done
}

_choice_plugin() {
    local d

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe skogai command runner: typed io for handing work to agents
#
# every agent call is `prompt + files -> json matching a schema`.
# pure by default: only `--apply` changes existing files, scaffolds only create new ones.
# @meta require-tools jq,yq,git,claude
# @meta dotenv
# @meta binname argc
# @env SKOGAI_MODEL=sonnet                         default model for agent calls
# @env ARGC_DOCS=~/.local/src/argc/docs           argc docs handed to `improve`
# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$PWD"
PLUGINS="$ROOT/plugins"
SCHEMAS="$PLUGINS/skogai-runner/schemas"
WORKORDERS="$ROOT/.skogai/workorders"
LOGS="$ROOT/.skogai/logs/argc"

# @cmd send a prompt and files to an agent, print its typed output
#
# the prompt comes from --prompt or stdin. files are inlined as
# <file path="..."> blocks, so the agent needs no tools to read them.
# with --schema stdout is the json object, without it plain text.
# @option -p --prompt                  prompt text, read from stdin if omitted
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            file to inline
# @option -s --schema[?`_choice_schema`] schema name or path for the output
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to $SKOGAI_MODEL
# @option -t --tools                   tools the agent may use, none if omitted
# @option -a --allow*                  allowed tool patterns, e.g. "Bash(git log *)"
# @option    --plugin-dir* <DIR>       plugin to load into the agent
# @flag      --raw                     print the full result envelope
# @alias s
send() {
    local prompt="${argc_prompt:-$(cat)}"
    _compose "$prompt" "${argc_file[@]}" |
        _agent "${argc_schema:-}" "${argc_model:-$SKOGAI_MODEL}" "${argc_tools:-}" "${argc_raw:-}"
}

# @cmd ask an agent to edit files, print the patch. pure unless --apply
#
# the agent returns whole files (schema `edit`), the patch is derived
# here with `git diff`, so a bad hunk header can never break it.
# @arg request~                        what to change
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            files to hand over, default Argcfile.sh and the runner skill
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to $SKOGAI_MODEL
# @flag      --apply                   apply the patch to the tree
# @alias i
improve() {
    local files=("${argc_file[@]}")
    [[ ${#files[@]} -gt 0 ]] || files=(Argcfile.sh plugins/skogai-runner/skills/argc/SKILL.md)
    local docs="${ARGC_DOCS/#\~/$HOME}"
    local ctx=()
    [[ -f "$docs/specification.md" ]] && ctx+=("$docs/specification.md")
    [[ -f "$docs/command-runner.md" ]] && ctx+=("$docs/command-runner.md")

    local prompt
    prompt="$(printf '%s\n\n%s\n%s\n' "${argc_request[*]}" \
        "return every file you change in full, paths relative to the repo root." \
        "only these files may change: ${files[*]}")"

    local out patch
    out="$(_compose "$prompt" "${files[@]}" "${ctx[@]}" | _agent edit "${argc_model:-$SKOGAI_MODEL}" "" "")"
    patch="$(_edit_to_patch "$out" "${files[@]}")"
    jq -r '.summary' <<<"$out" >&2
    if [[ -z "$patch" ]]; then
        echo "empty patch" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "${argc_apply:-}" ]]; then
        git apply --check <<<"$patch"
        git apply <<<"$patch"
        git diff --stat -- "${files[@]}" >&2
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$patch"
        return 1
    fi
}

# @cmd workorders: one bounded question, gathered inputs, checkable output
wo() { :; }

# @cmd scaffold a workorder
# @arg name!                           kebab-case name
# @option -s --schema[?`_choice_schema`] output schema, default answer
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            input files
# @option -t --tools                   tools the worker may use
wo::new() {
    local path="$WORKORDERS/$argc_name.md"
    [[ ! -e "$path" ]] || { echo "exists: $path" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$WORKORDERS"
    {
        echo "---"
        echo "type: workorder"
        echo "title: $argc_name"
        echo "schema: ${argc_schema:-answer}"
        echo "tools: \"${argc_tools:-}\""
        echo "files:"
        local f
        for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do echo "  - $f"; done
        echo "---"
        echo
        echo "<one bounded question>"
    } >"$path"
    echo "$path"
}

# @cmd run a workorder, write <name>.result.json beside it
# @arg workorder![`_choice_workorder`] name or path
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to the workorder's or $SKOGAI_MODEL
wo::run() {
    local path
    path="$(_workorder_path "$argc_workorder")"
    local fm
    fm="$(yq --front-matter=extract -o json '.' "$path")"
    [[ "$(jq -r '.type' <<<"$fm")" == workorder ]] || { echo "not a workorder: $path" >&2; return 2; }

    local files=() f
    while IFS= read -r f; do [[ -n "$f" ]] && files+=("$f"); done < <(jq -r '.files // [] | .[]' <<<"$fm")
    local schema model tools
    schema="$(jq -r '.schema // "answer"' <<<"$fm")"
    model="${argc_model:-$(jq -r --arg d "$SKOGAI_MODEL" '.model // $d' <<<"$fm")}"
    tools="$(jq -r '.tools // ""' <<<"$fm")"

    local result="${path%.md}.result.json"
    _compose "$(_body "$path")" "${files[@]}" | _agent "$schema" "$model" "$tools" "" >"$result"
    cat "$result"
}

# @cmd list workorders and whether they have a result
wo::ls() {
    local f
    for f in "$WORKORDERS"/*.md; do
        [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
        if [[ -e "${f%.md}.result.json" ]]; then echo "done  $(basename "$f" .md)"; else echo "open  $(basename "$f" .md)"; fi
    done
}

# @cmd claude code plugins under plugins/
plugin() { :; }

# @cmd scaffold a plugin with one skill
# @arg name!                           kebab-case name
# @arg description!                    one line: what it is for
plugin::new() {
    local dir="$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
    [[ ! -e "$dir" ]] || { echo "exists: $dir" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude-plugin" "$dir/skills/$argc_name"
    jq -n --arg n "$argc_name" --arg d "$argc_description" \
        '{name: $n, version: "0.1.0", description: $d, author: {name: "skogix"}}' >"$dir/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
    printf -- '---\nname: %s\ndescription: %s\n---\n\n# %s\n' \
        "$argc_name" "$argc_description" "$argc_name" >"$dir/skills/$argc_name/SKILL.md"
    echo "$dir"
}

# @cmd validate plugins, all if no name is given
# @arg name*[`_choice_plugin`]
plugin::check() {
    local names=("${argc_name[@]}") n
    [[ ${#names[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t names < <(_choice_plugin)
    for n in "${names[@]}"; do claude plugin validate "$PLUGINS/$n"; done
}

# @cmd run a plugin's evals
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]
plugin::eval() {
    claude plugin eval "$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
}

# @cmd hand a plugin to an agent for improvement, pure unless --apply
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]
# @arg request~                        what to change
# @flag --apply                        apply the patch to the tree
plugin::improve() {
    local files=()
    mapfile -t files < <(git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard "plugins/$argc_name")
    argc_file=("${files[@]}")
    improve
}

# @cmd session journals (.skogai/journal.md): read them back, harvest them
journal() { :; }

# @cmd only the user's input, one json row per turn
# @arg file[`_choice_journal`]         journal, default .skogai/journal.md
# @option --last <N>                   only the last N turns
# @flag   --md                         markdown instead of json rows
journal::prompts() {
    local file="${argc_file:-$ROOT/.skogai/journal.md}"
    local rows
    rows="$(_journal_slice "$file" "${argc_last:-0}" | awk '
        function flush() { if (turn != "") printf "%s\037%s\037%s\036", ts, turn, prompt; prompt = "" }
        /^## [0-9]{4}-/ { flush(); ts = $2 " " $3; turn = $NF; sec = ""; next }
        /^\*\*User\*\*$/ { sec = "user"; next }
        /^\*\*(Assistant|Actions)\*\*$/ { sec = ""; next }
        sec == "user" && /^>/ { sub(/^> ?/, ""); prompt = prompt (prompt == "" ? "" : "\n") $0 }
        END { flush() }' |
        jq -Rsc 'split("\u001e")[:-1][] | split("\u001f") | {ts: .[0], turn: .[1], prompt: .[2]}')"
    if [[ -n "${argc_md:-}" ]]; then
        jq -r '"## \(.ts) · turn \(.turn)\n\n\(.prompt)\n"' <<<"$rows"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$rows"
    fi
}

# @cmd agents pick decisions, docs, todos and learnings out of a journal
#
# the journal is cut into chunks of --turns turns, each chunk goes to one
# worker with schema `harvest`. stdout is one json array of every item.
# @arg file[`_choice_journal`]         journal, default .skogai/journal.md
# @option --last <N>                   only the last N turns
# @option --turns <N>                  turns per chunk, default 20
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to $SKOGAI_MODEL
journal::harvest() {
    local file="${argc_file:-$ROOT/.skogai/journal.md}"
    local per="${argc_turns:-20}"
    local dir
    dir="$(mktemp -d)"
    trap 'rm -rf "$dir"' RETURN
    _journal_slice "$file" "${argc_last:-0}" |
        awk -v per="$per" -v dir="$dir" '/^## [0-9]{4}-/ && n++ % per == 0 { out = sprintf("%s/%03d.md", dir, n / per) } out { print > out }'

    local prompt
    prompt="$(cat <<'EOF'
the file is a slice of a session journal: turns between a user and an assistant.
pick out what is worth keeping after the session:
- decision: something settled, with why
- doc: how something works now, worth writing down
- todo: still open at the end of the slice
- learning: a gotcha or rule found the hard way
skip chatter, anything superseded later in the slice, and anything only true for that conversation.
turn is the id after "turn" in the heading where it was settled. an empty list is fine.
EOF
)"
    local chunk
    for chunk in "$dir"/*.md; do
        echo "harvest $(basename "$chunk") ($(grep -c '^## [0-9]' "$chunk") turns)" >&2
        _compose "$prompt" "$chunk" | _agent harvest "${argc_model:-$SKOGAI_MODEL}" "" "" >"${chunk%.md}.json"
    done
    jq -s '[.[].items[]]' "$dir"/*.json
}

# @cmd static checks on the runner itself: argc parse, shellcheck, schemas, plugins
check() {
    argc --argc-export Argcfile.sh >/dev/null && echo "ok    argc parse"
    if command -v shellcheck >/dev/null; then
        shellcheck -x Argcfile.sh && echo "ok    shellcheck"
    else
        echo "skip  shellcheck: not installed"
    fi
    local s
    for s in "$SCHEMAS"/*.json; do jq -e . "$s" >/dev/null && echo "ok    schema $(basename "$s")"; done
    plugin::check
}

# prompt + files -> one message
_compose() {
    local prompt="$1"
    shift
    printf '<prompt>\n%s\n</prompt>\n' "$prompt"
    local f
    for f in "$@"; do
        [[ -f "$f" ]] || { echo "no such file: $f" >&2; return 2; }
        printf '\n<file path="%s">\n%s\n</file>\n' "$f" "$(cat "$f")"
    done
}

# message on stdin -> typed output on stdout, envelope logged
# _agent <schema> <model> <tools> <raw>
_agent() {
    local schema="$1" model="$2" tools="$3" raw="$4"
    local args=(-p --output-format json --model "$model" --tools "$tools" --permission-mode dontAsk)
    local a
    for a in "${argc_allow[@]}"; do args+=(--allowedTools "$a"); done
    for a in "${argc_plugin_dir[@]}"; do args+=(--plugin-dir "$a"); done
    [[ -n "$schema" ]] && args+=(--json-schema "$(jq -c . "$(_schema_path "$schema")")")

    mkdir -p "$LOGS"
    local log
    log="$LOGS/$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)-$$.json"
    claude "${args[@]}" >"$log"

    if [[ -n "$raw" ]]; then cat "$log"; fi
    if [[ "$(jq -r '.is_error' "$log")" == true ]]; then
        jq -r '.result // .subtype' "$log" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    [[ -n "$raw" ]] && return 0
    if [[ -n "$schema" ]]; then jq '.structured_output' "$log"; else jq -r '.result' "$log"; fi
}

# edit json + allowed files -> unified diff, refusing paths outside the list
_edit_to_patch() {
    local out="$1"
    shift
    local new path allowed f
    new="$(mktemp)"
    trap 'rm -f "$new"' RETURN
    while IFS= read -r path; do
        allowed=
        for f in "$@"; do [[ "$path" == "$f" ]] && allowed=1; done
        [[ -n "$allowed" ]] || { echo "refused: $path is not a handed-over file" >&2; return 2; }
        jq -j --arg p "$path" '.files[] | select(.path == $p) | .content' <<<"$out" >"$new"
        diff -u --label "a/$path" --label "b/$path" "$path" "$new" || true
    done < <(jq -r '.files[].path' <<<"$out")
}

_body() { awk 'NR==1 && /^---$/ {fm=1; next} fm && /^---$/ {fm=0; next} !fm' "$1"; }

_schema_path() {
    if [[ -f "$1" ]]; then echo "$1"; else echo "$SCHEMAS/$1.json"; fi
}

_workorder_path() {
    if [[ -f "$1" ]]; then echo "$1"; else echo "$WORKORDERS/$1.md"; fi
}

_choice_schema() {
    local f
    for f in "$SCHEMAS"/*.json; do basename "$f" .json; done
}

_choice_workorder() {
    local f
    for f in "$WORKORDERS"/*.md; do [[ -e "$f" ]] && basename "$f" .md; done
}

_choice_plugin() {
    local d
    for d in "$PLUGINS"/*/.claude-plugin; do basename "$(dirname "$d")"; done
}

eval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"

skogix's words: "you will be the one writing context, your intentions and will be the one managing yourself". this is the first iteration of that: your own command runner, the same commands everywhere, for handing strictly typed work to other agents. start by making it self-improving, so agents do the heavy lifting.

## what it is

- `Argcfile.sh`: recipes, all built on `send :: (prompt, [file], schema) -> json` (`claude -p --json-schema`, read `.structured_output`).
- `plugins/skogai-runner/`: skill `argc` (how to use and extend the runner) and schemas `answer`, `edit`, `check`.
- `workorders/smoke-test.*`: a worked example, a workorder and its typed result.
- `TODO.md`: what's needed before it runs here.

usage is in `plugins/skogai-runner/skills/argc/SKILL.md`, and `argc --help` is the source of truth.

## decisions

- **pure by default**: `improve` prints a patch and exits `1`, like `skogai plan`. only `--apply` writes. scaffolds (`wo new`, `plugin new`) create new files and refuse to overwrite.
- **whole files, derived patch**: workers return complete files (schema `edit`), and the runner builds the diff with `diff -u`, so a bad hunk from a model can't happen. paths not handed over are refused.
- **no tools by default**: inputs are inlined as `<file path>` blocks. `--tools` opts in.
- **workorders are blobs of text**: markdown, frontmatter for `schema`/`files`/`tools`. they go wherever we want.

# argc

`argc` runs recipes from the nearest `Argcfile.sh` up the tree, so the same commands work from any directory in the repo. `argc --help` and `argc <cmd> --help` are the source of truth; this skill only says how to use them.

## the contract

the agent call behind `send` is one function:

```
send :: (prompt, [file], schema) -> json
```

- files are inlined, the worker gets no tools unless `--tools` says so.
- `--schema` names a file in `plugins/skogai-runner/schemas/` or a path. stdout is the json object; envelopes are logged to `.skogai/logs/argc/`.
- exit `0` ok or empty patch, `1` agent error or a patch printed but not applied (like `skogai plan`), `2` usage.

## recipes

| recipe | use |
|---|---|
| `argc send -p <q> -f <file>... -s answer` | one bounded question, short checkable answer |
| `argc send -s check -f <file>...` | findings as `{path, line, rule, severity, message}` |
| `argc improve <request> [-f file]... [--apply]` | whole-file edits from a worker, patch derived by `diff -u`. prints the patch unless `--apply` |
| `argc wo new <name> -s <schema> -f <file>...` | write `.skogai/workorders/<name>.md` |
| `argc wo run <name>` | run it, result in `<name>.result.json` |
| `argc plugin new <name> <description>` | scaffold `plugins/<name>` |
| `argc plugin check [name]`, `argc plugin eval <name>` | validate, run evals |
| `argc plugin improve <name> <request> [--apply]` | `improve` over every file of a plugin |
| `argc journal prompts [file] [--last N] [--md]` | only the user's input from a session journal, one json row per turn |
| `argc journal harvest [file] [--last N] [--turns N]` | workers pick decisions, docs, todos, learnings out of a journal (schema `harvest`) |
| `argc check` | argc parse, shellcheck, schemas, plugins |

## workorders

one bounded question per workorder. inputs are listed as files, never "go look around". output is a schema, so the result is checkable without reading prose.

```markdown
---
type: workorder
title: <name>
schema: answer
tools: ""
files:
  - path/to/input.md
---

<one bounded question>
```

## extending the runner

a recipe is a bash function with `# @cmd` above it; `foo::bar` is `argc foo bar`. flags and options become `$argc_<name>`. spec: `~/.local/src/argc/docs/specification.md`.

- pure by default. a recipe that writes takes `--apply`, and without it prints what it would do.
- a missing recipe is a gap: add it, or run `argc improve "<what it should do>"` and review the patch.
- keep a new schema small, `additionalProperties: false`, every field required.
- run `argc check` after a change.

input.last_assistant_message:
I cleaned up paths first and committed that. Overall the runner is solid. **Yes, make it a plugin for use outside this repo**, but first split what any repo can use from what only fits this marketplace.

## Paths fixed (committed)
- `argc/workorders/smoke-test.*` → `.skogai/workorders/`. The runner looks up workorders there, so `argc wo run smoke-test` couldn't find it by name. It now shows up as `done` in `argc wo ls`.
- `argc/HANDOVER.md` and `argc/TODO.md` → `plugins/skogai-runner/`. I fixed the workorder path in the handover. In the TODO I ticked `.gitignore` and the mise tools: `.skogai/logs/` is already ignored, and argc and shellcheck are in your mise config.
- `argc/plugins/` became `argc/docs/` and was staged while I was working, so I left those docs alone. Once they settle, `ARGC_DOCS` should point at them. Its default is `~/.local/src/argc/docs`, which only has 3 of the 7 files.

## What it does
`Argcfile.sh` wraps a single call: prompt + files inlined as `<file>` blocks → `claude -p --json-schema` → `.structured_output`. Every recipe is built on that:
- **`send`**: one-shot typed question.
- **`improve`**: the agent returns whole files and the runner builds the diff itself. It refuses files you didn't hand over and only writes with `--apply`. This is the best idea in the runner.
- **`wo`**: workorders, which are frontmatter plus one question, with a result written beside them.
- **`journal`**: extracts your prompts from a session journal, and has agents pull decisions, docs, todos and learnings out of it.
- **`plugin` and `check`**: helpers specific to this marketplace.

`argc check` passes: the argc parse, shellcheck and all 4 schemas.

## Problems worth fixing
1. **A failed `wo run` counts as done.** `> "$result"` creates the result file before the agent finishes. If the agent fails, an empty `.result.json` is left behind and `wo ls` reports `done`. Fix: write to a temp file, then `mv` it into place on success.
2. **Agent errors give no message.** `claude` exits 1 on error, which I confirmed. Because of `set -e`, the script stops at `claude ... >"$log"` before the `is_error` branch prints `.result`, so the error only exists in the log. Fix: `claude ... >"$log" || true`.
3. **Paths only work in this repo.** `ROOT="$PWD"` and `-f` paths resolve from the Argcfile's directory, not the caller's (both are already in the TODO). `SCHEMAS` is hard-wired to `plugins/skogai-runner/schemas`.
4. **Small issues:**
   - `send` with no `-p` and nothing piped in hangs on `cat`.
   - `_compose` strips trailing newlines, and a file that contains `</file>` breaks the framing.
   - `plugin new` hard-codes `author: skogix`.

## How to make it a plugin
- **Generic core goes in the plugin:** `send`, `improve`, `wo`, `journal`, the schemas and the argc docs, in `plugins/skogai-runner/scripts/Argcfile.sh`.
  - Resolve schemas from the script's real path.
  - Resolve caller files against `$ARGC_PWD`.
  - Keep `.skogai/` as the per-project state dir.
- **Don't use a top-level `bin/`.** The docs say claude.ai org sync rejects plugins that have one (`docs/plugins/host-marketplace.md:94`). The skill should run the script via `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/`, for example with `argc --argc-run`, or call a wrapper kept outside `bin/`.
- **Repo-local recipes stay here:** `plugin new/check/eval/improve` and `check` remain in a thin root `Argcfile.sh` that calls the core.

That split also clears two of the TODO items: placing the Argcfile and the `$ARGC_PWD` fix. If you want it, I can do the split plus fixes 1 and 2 once you're done with `argc/docs`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe skogai command runner: typed io for handing work to agents
#
# every agent call is `prompt + files -> json matching a schema`.
# pure by default: only `--apply` changes existing files, scaffolds only create new ones.
# @meta require-tools jq,yq,git,claude
# @meta dotenv
# @meta binname argc
# @env SKOGAI_MODEL=sonnet                         default model for agent calls
# @env ARGC_DOCS=~/.local/src/argc/docs           argc docs handed to `improve`
# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$PWD"
PLUGINS="$ROOT/plugins"
SCHEMAS="$PLUGINS/skogai-runner/schemas"
WORKORDERS="$ROOT/.skogai/workorders"
LOGS="$ROOT/.skogai/logs/argc"

# @cmd send a prompt and files to an agent, print its typed output
#
# the prompt comes from --prompt or stdin. files are inlined as
# <file path="..."> blocks, so the agent needs no tools to read them.
# with --schema stdout is the json object, without it plain text.
# @option -p --prompt                  prompt text, read from stdin if omitted
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            file to inline
# @option -s --schema[?`_choice_schema`] schema name or path for the output
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to $SKOGAI_MODEL
# @option -t --tools                   tools the agent may use, none if omitted
# @option -a --allow*                  allowed tool patterns, e.g. "Bash(git log *)"
# @option    --plugin-dir* <DIR>       plugin to load into the agent
# @flag      --raw                     print the full result envelope
# @alias s
send() {
    local prompt="${argc_prompt:-$(cat)}"
    _compose "$prompt" "${argc_file[@]}" |
        _agent "${argc_schema:-}" "${argc_model:-$SKOGAI_MODEL}" "${argc_tools:-}" "${argc_raw:-}"
}

# @cmd ask an agent to edit files, print the patch. pure unless --apply
#
# the agent returns whole files (schema `edit`), the patch is derived
# here with `git diff`, so a bad hunk header can never break it.
# @arg request~                        what to change
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            files to hand over, default Argcfile.sh and the runner skill
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to $SKOGAI_MODEL
# @flag      --apply                   apply the patch to the tree
# @alias i
improve() {
    local files=("${argc_file[@]}")
    [[ ${#files[@]} -gt 0 ]] || files=(Argcfile.sh plugins/skogai-runner/skills/argc/SKILL.md)
    local docs="${ARGC_DOCS/#\~/$HOME}"
    local ctx=()
    [[ -f "$docs/specification.md" ]] && ctx+=("$docs/specification.md")
    [[ -f "$docs/command-runner.md" ]] && ctx+=("$docs/command-runner.md")

    local prompt
    prompt="$(printf '%s\n\n%s\n%s\n' "${argc_request[*]}" \
        "return every file you change in full, paths relative to the repo root." \
        "only these files may change: ${files[*]}")"

    local out patch
    out="$(_compose "$prompt" "${files[@]}" "${ctx[@]}" | _agent edit "${argc_model:-$SKOGAI_MODEL}" "" "")"
    patch="$(_edit_to_patch "$out" "${files[@]}")"
    jq -r '.summary' <<<"$out" >&2
    if [[ -z "$patch" ]]; then
        echo "empty patch" >&2

# @cmd workorders: one bounded question, gathered inputs, checkable output
wo() { :; }

# @cmd scaffold a workorder
# @arg name!                           kebab-case name
# @option -s --schema[?`_choice_schema`] output schema, default answer
# @option -f --file* <FILE>            input files
# @option -t --tools                   tools the worker may use
wo::new() {
    local path="$WORKORDERS/$argc_name.md"
    [[ ! -e "$path" ]] || { echo "exists: $path" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$WORKORDERS"
    {
        echo "---"
        echo "type: workorder"
        echo "title: $argc_name"
        echo "schema: ${argc_schema:-answer}"
        echo "tools: \"${argc_tools:-}\""
        echo "files:"
        local f
        for f in "${argc_file[@]}"; do echo "  - $f"; done
        echo "---"
        echo
        echo "<one bounded question>"
    } >"$path"
    echo "$path"
}

# @cmd run a workorder, write <name>.result.json beside it
# @arg workorder![`_choice_workorder`] name or path
# @option -m --model                   model, defaults to the workorder's or $SKOGAI_MODEL
wo::run() {
    local path
    path="$(_workorder_path "$argc_workorder")"
    local fm
    fm="$(yq --front-matter=extract -o json '.' "$path")"
    [[ "$(jq -r '.type' <<<"$fm")" == workorder ]] || { echo "not a workorder: $path" >&2; return 2; }

    local files=() f
    while IFS= read -r f; do [[ -n "$f" ]] && files+=("$f"); done < <(jq -r '.files // [] | .[]' <<<"$fm")
    local schema model tools
    schema="$(jq -r '.schema // "answer"' <<<"$fm")"
    model="${argc_model:-$(jq -r --arg d "$SKOGAI_MODEL" '.model // $d' <<<"$fm")}"
    tools="$(jq -r '.tools // ""' <<<"$fm")"

    local result="${path%.md}.result.json"
    _compose "$(_body "$path")" "${files[@]}" | _agent "$schema" "$model" "$tools" "" >"$result"
    cat "$result"
}

# @cmd list workorders and whether they have a result
wo::ls() {
    local f
    for f in "$WORKORDERS"/*.md; do
        [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
        if [[ -e "${f%.md}.result.json" ]]; then echo "done  $(basename "$f" .md)"; else echo "open  $(basename "$f" .md)"; fi
    done
}

# @cmd claude code plugins under plugins/
plugin() { :; }

# @cmd scaffold a plugin with one skill
# @arg name!                           kebab-case name
# @arg description!                    one line: what it is for
plugin::new() {
    local dir="$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
    [[ ! -e "$dir" ]] || { echo "exists: $dir" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude-plugin" "$dir/skills/$argc_name"
    jq -n --arg n "$argc_name" --arg d "$argc_description" \
        '{name: $n, version: "0.1.0", description: $d, author: {name: "skogix"}}' >"$dir/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
    printf -- '---\nname: %s\ndescription: %s\n---\n\n# %s\n' \
        "$argc_name" "$argc_description" "$argc_name" >"$dir/skills/$argc_name/SKILL.md"
    echo "$dir"
}

# @cmd validate plugins, all if no name is given
# @arg name*[`_choice_plugin`]
plugin::check() {
    local names=("${argc_name[@]}") n
    [[ ${#names[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t names < <(_choice_plugin)
    for n in "${names[@]}"; do claude plugin validate "$PLUGINS/$n"; done
}

# @cmd run a plugin's evals
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]

# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]

## Check which stage a plugin reached

An `enabledPlugins` entry becomes a plugin you can use in stages: your settings declare it, Claude Code fetches it to disk, and the running session loads it. When a plugin doesn't behave as a settings file suggests, check which stage it reached:

* **Declared, in settings**: `enabledPlugins` says which plugins should be on, and `extraKnownMarketplaces` says which marketplaces should exist. When you run `claude plugin marketplace add`, Claude Code writes the marketplace to `extraKnownMarketplaces` in your user settings as well as to disk
* **Fetched, on disk under `~/.claude/plugins/`**: the records of what Claude Code has fetched, and the fetched files themselves:
  * `known_marketplaces.json` records each marketplace Claude Code has fetched, with its `source`, `installLocation`, `lastUpdated`, and `autoUpdate`. There is one `known_marketplaces.json` per user, so a marketplace you add in one project is available in every project
  * `installed_plugins.json` records each install with its `scope`, `installPath`, and `version`
  * `cache/` holds the plugin files
* **Loaded, in the running session**: the plugin set Claude Code loaded at startup or at the last `/reload-plugins`. Changes to settings or to disk don't reach this layer until you run `/reload-plugins` or start a new session. That is why `claude plugin update` ends with `Restart to apply changes.` and background updates prompt you with `Run /reload-plugins to apply`

### Plugins and marketplaces that aren't on disk at session start

Plugins load at session start from `installed_plugins.json` and the cache without using the network. After the session starts, Claude Code checks the declared marketplaces in the background:

* **A marketplace that settings declare but `known_marketplaces.json` lacks**: Claude Code clones it, then reloads plugins and downloads enabled plugins that aren't cached yet
* **A declared marketplace whose source changed in settings**: Claude Code re-fetches it from the new source and shows `Plugins changed. Run /reload-plugins to activate.`

An enabled plugin that neither path fetched and that has no usable cache directory shows `Plugin "<name>" not cached at <path>` in the `/plugin` **Errors** tab, and `claude plugin list` adds `— run /plugin to refresh` to the same line. For the fix, see [`Plugin "<name>" not cached at <path>`](/docs/en/plugins/troubleshooting#plugin-not-cached-at).

## Find where a plugin came from

Every plugin has an id of the form `<name>@<origin>`, which is what you see in settings files and in `claude plugin list --json`. The part after `@` tells you where Claude Code found the plugin:

### Keep plugin files out of Git LFS

Keep the files your plugins need out of [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com). When users add a marketplace hosted in a git repository, or install a git-based plugin it lists, Claude Code clones that marketplace or plugin repository onto their machine. The clone never downloads LFS content, so LFS-tracked files arrive as pointer files.

### Share files within a marketplace with symlinks

To share files between your plugin and other parts of the same marketplace, create symbolic links inside your plugin directory. When Claude Code copies the plugin into its cache, it handles each symlink by where the target resolves:

* **Within the plugin's own directory**: the symlink is preserved as a relative symlink in the cache, so it keeps resolving to the copied target at runtime.
* **Elsewhere within the same marketplace**: the symlink is dereferenced. The target's content is copied into the cache in its place. This lets a meta-plugin's `skills/` directory link to skills defined by other plugins in the marketplace.
* **Outside the marketplace**: the symlink is skipped for security.

For plugins installed from a local path, or from a [`command` source](/docs/en/plugins/marketplace-reference#command-plugin-source) whose `mode` is the default `copy`, Claude Code preserves only symlinks that resolve within the plugin's own directory and skips all others.

# Argc Macros

Argc macros are used to change compgen behavior.

## __argc_filter=

Completions not starting with filter will be ignored

```sh
echo "__argc_filter=$ARGC_CWORD"
```

## __argc_prefix=

Add prefix to completion

```sh
echo "__argc_prefix=--foo="
```

## __argc_suffix=

Add suffix to completion

```sh
echo -e "__argc_prefix=:\0"
```

## __argc_value=path

Complete a path

```sh
echo __argc_value=path
echo __argc_value=path:.json,jsonc    # Accept only json/jsonc file
```

If the path is obviously a file, use `__argc_value=file` in preference.

```sh
echo __argc_value=file 
echo __argc_value=file:.json,jsonc    # Accept only json/jsonc file
```

## __argc_value=dir

Complete a dir

```sh
echo "__argc_value=dir"
```

## __argc_cd

Change current dir

```sh
echo "__argc_cd=$argc_cwd"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe skogai main runner: one `argc` for every registered command file
#
# `argc <name> ...` runs the argc script registered as <name>, from the directory
# argc was called in. `argc register <file> <name>` adds one, `argc sync` rebuilds.
# this file is a template: `sync` writes ~/Argcfile.sh from it plus one recipe
# per registered command, so argc finds it from anywhere under ~.
# @meta require-tools argc,jq
# @meta binname argc
# @env ARGC_COMMANDS                             registry dir, default ~/.config/argc/commands
# @env ARGC_MAIN                                 the generated main file, default ~/Argcfile.sh

# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval
set -euo pipefail

COMMANDS="${ARGC_COMMANDS:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/argc/commands}"
MAIN="${ARGC_MAIN:-$HOME/Argcfile.sh}"
TEMPLATE="$(realpath "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
# >>> template
# <<< template

# @cmd register an argc script as `argc <name>`, then sync
# @arg file!                           the argc script, linked, not copied
# @arg name!                           lowercase, one segment
register() {
    [[ "$argc_name" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ ]] || { echo "bad name: $argc_name" >&2; return 2; }
    local file
    file="$(realpath "$ARGC_PWD/$argc_file" 2>/dev/null || realpath "$argc_file")"
    argc --argc-export "$file" >/dev/null
    mkdir -p "$COMMANDS"
    ln -sfn "$file" "$COMMANDS/$argc_name.sh"
    sync
}

# @cmd remove a registered command, then sync
# @arg name![`_choice_command`]
unregister() {
    rm -f "$COMMANDS/$argc_name.sh"
    sync
}

# @cmd registered commands and where they point
ls() {
    local f
    for f in "$COMMANDS"/*.sh; do
        [[ -e "$f" || -L "$f" ]] || continue
        printf '%-12s %s\n' "$(basename "$f" .sh)" "$(readlink "$f")"
    done
}

# @cmd rebuild the main file from the template and the registry
#
# a command whose file is gone or doesn't parse is skipped with a warning.
sync() {
    local out f name describe
    out="$(mktemp)"
    {
        sed '/^# >>> template$/q' "$TEMPLATE"
        printf 'TEMPLATE=%q\n' "$TEMPLATE"
        sed -n '/^# <<< template$/,$p' "$TEMPLATE" | sed '/^eval "\$(argc --argc-eval/d'
        for f in "$COMMANDS"/*.sh; do
            [[ -e "$f" ]] || { [[ -L "$f" ]] && echo "skip  $(basename "$f"): $(readlink "$f") is gone" >&2; continue; }
            name="$(basename "$f" .sh)"
            describe="$(argc --argc-export "$f" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.describe | split("\n")[0]')" ||
                { echo "skip  $name: does not parse" >&2; continue; }
            printf '\n# @cmd %s\n# @arg args~[`_choice_delegate`]\n%s() { _delegate %s "${argc_args[@]}"; }\n' \
                "${describe:-$name}" "$name" "$name"
        done
        printf '\neval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"\n'
    } >"$out"
    argc --argc-export "$out" >/dev/null
    mv "$out" "$MAIN"
    echo "wrote $MAIN" >&2
}

# registered command <name> with the rest of the args, from the caller's directory
_delegate() {
    local name="$1"
    shift
    (cd "${ARGC_PWD:-$PWD}" && argc --argc-run "$COMMANDS/$name.sh" "$@")
}

# completion for a forwarded command: ask its own script, drop argc's color field
_choice_delegate() {
    local name="$argc__cmd_fn"
    argc --argc-compgen generic "$COMMANDS/$name.sh" "$name" "${argc__args[@]:argc__cmd_arg_index+1}" |
        awk -F '\t' 'NF >= 3 && $2 ~ /^\/color:/ { print $1 "\t" $3; next } { print }'
}

_choice_command() {
    local f
    for f in "$COMMANDS"/*.sh; do [[ -e "$f" ]] && basename "$f" .sh; done
}

eval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"

**How it works**
- **Registering:** `argc register <file> <name>` links the script into `~/.config/argc/commands/<name>.sh`, then runs `sync`. `argc unregister <name>` removes it and `argc ls` lists what's registered.
- **`sync`:** rebuilds `~/Argcfile.sh` from the template, with one recipe per registered script.
  - Each recipe's description comes from that script's `@describe`, read with `argc --argc-export`.
  - A script that is missing or fails to parse is skipped with a warning.
  - The new file is parsed before it replaces the old one, so a broken script can't break `argc`.
- **Running a command:** `argc runner wo ls` runs `runner.sh` from the directory you called it in. `argc runner wo --help` shows the script's own help.
- **Tab completion:** passed on to the script itself via `argc --argc-compgen`, so subcommands, schema names and file paths all complete through the main file.
- **Updating the template:** `~/Argcfile.sh` is generated output, so changes to `main.sh` take effect on the next `sync`.

**Things to know before installing**
- argc uses the nearest `Argcfile.sh` above the current directory. Inside a repo that has its own (like this marketplace), that file wins, so `argc runner` isn't available there unless the repo's file forwards it. Here the repo's `send`, `wo` and so on already do the same job.
- Registered scripts are links, so `runner` should point at your local checkout, not the plugin cache, whose path changes with every version.
- Plugins could register themselves from a session-start hook, but that conflicts with your "offer, don't install" rule, so for now registration is something you run yourself.

argc --argc-run plugins/skogai-runner/scripts/main.sh register plugins/skogai-runner/scripts/runner.sh runner

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe skogai-marketplace: scaffold, validate, eval and improve its plugins
#
# works on the marketplace checkout this script lives in, from any directory.
# register it with the main runner as `argc marketplace`.
# @meta require-tools jq,git,claude
# @meta binname argc
# @env SKOGAI_MARKETPLACE_REPO_DIR               marketplace checkout, default the one holding this script

# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(dirname "$(realpath "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")"
REPO="${SKOGAI_MARKETPLACE_REPO_DIR:-$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)}"
PLUGINS="$REPO/plugins"
RUNNER="$HERE/runner.sh"

# @cmd scaffold a plugin with one skill
# @arg name!                           kebab-case name
# @arg description!                    one line: what it is for
new() {
    local dir="$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
    [[ ! -e "$dir" ]] || { echo "exists: $dir" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude-plugin" "$dir/skills/$argc_name"
    jq -n --arg n "$argc_name" --arg d "$argc_description" \
        '{name: $n, version: "0.1.0", description: $d, author: {name: "skogix"}}' >"$dir/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
    printf -- '---\nname: %s\ndescription: %s\n---\n\n# %s\n' \
        "$argc_name" "$argc_description" "$argc_name" >"$dir/skills/$argc_name/SKILL.md"
    echo "$dir"
}

# @cmd validate plugins, all if no name is given, then check marketplace.json is generated
# @arg name*[`_choice_plugin`]
check() {
    local names=("${argc_name[@]}") n
    [[ ${#names[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t names < <(_choice_plugin)
    for n in "${names[@]}"; do claude plugin validate "$PLUGINS/$n"; done
    "$REPO/scripts/generate-marketplace-json.sh" --check
}

# @cmd regenerate .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
json() {
    "$REPO/scripts/generate-marketplace-json.sh"
}

# @cmd run a plugin's evals
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]
eval() {
    claude plugin eval "$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
}

# @cmd hand a plugin to an agent for improvement, pure unless --apply
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]
# @arg request~                        what to change
# @flag --apply                        apply the patch to the tree
improve() {
    local args=("${argc_request[*]}") f
    while IFS= read -r f; do args+=(-f "$f"); done < <(git -C "$REPO" ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard "plugins/$argc_name")
    [[ -z "${argc_apply:-}" ]] || args+=(--apply)
    (cd "$REPO" && argc --argc-run "$RUNNER" improve "${args[@]}")
}

_choice_plugin() {
    local d
    for d in "$PLUGINS"/*/.claude-plugin; do basename "$(dirname "$d")"; done
}

builtin eval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @describe skogai-marketplace runner: the skogai-runner core plus recipes for plugins/
#
# send, improve, wo and journal forward to plugins/skogai-runner/scripts/runner.sh,
# run from the directory argc was called in. `argc <cmd> --help` shows the core's help.
# @meta require-tools jq,git,claude
# @meta dotenv
# @meta binname argc
# shellcheck disable=SC2154 # argc_* are assigned by --argc-eval
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(dirname "$(realpath "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")"
PLUGINS="$HERE/plugins"
CORE="$PLUGINS/skogai-runner/scripts/runner.sh"

# @cmd send a prompt and files to an agent, print its typed output
# @arg args~
# @alias s
send() { _core send "${argc_args[@]}"; }

# @cmd ask an agent to edit files, print the patch. pure unless --apply
# @arg args~
# @alias i
improve() { _core improve "${argc_args[@]}"; }

# @cmd workorders: new, run, ls
# @arg args~
wo() { _core wo "${argc_args[@]}"; }

# @cmd session journals: prompts, harvest
# @arg args~
journal() { _core journal "${argc_args[@]}"; }

# @cmd the runner's own checks, then every plugin
check() {
    _core check
    plugin::check
}

# @cmd claude code plugins under plugins/
plugin() { :; }

# @cmd scaffold a plugin with one skill
# @arg name!                           kebab-case name
# @arg description!                    one line: what it is for
plugin::new() {
    local dir="$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
    [[ ! -e "$dir" ]] || { echo "exists: $dir" >&2; return 2; }
    mkdir -p "$dir/.claude-plugin" "$dir/skills/$argc_name"
    jq -n --arg n "$argc_name" --arg d "$argc_description" \
        '{name: $n, version: "0.1.0", description: $d, author: {name: "skogix"}}' >"$dir/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
    printf -- '---\nname: %s\ndescription: %s\n---\n\n# %s\n' \
        "$argc_name" "$argc_description" "$argc_name" >"$dir/skills/$argc_name/SKILL.md"
    echo "$dir"
}

# @cmd validate plugins, all if no name is given
# @arg name*[`_choice_plugin`]
plugin::check() {
    local names=("${argc_name[@]}") n
    [[ ${#names[@]} -gt 0 ]] || mapfile -t names < <(_choice_plugin)
    for n in "${names[@]}"; do claude plugin validate "$PLUGINS/$n"; done
}

# @cmd run a plugin's evals
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]
plugin::eval() {
    claude plugin eval "$PLUGINS/$argc_name"
}

# @cmd hand a plugin to an agent for improvement, pure unless --apply
# @arg name![`_choice_plugin`]
# @arg request~                        what to change
# @flag --apply                        apply the patch to the tree
plugin::improve() {
    local args=("${argc_request[*]}") f
    while IFS= read -r f; do args+=(-f "$f"); done < <(git -C "$HERE" ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard "plugins/$argc_name")
    [[ -z "${argc_apply:-}" ]] || args+=(--apply)
    (cd "$HERE" && argc --argc-run "$CORE" improve "${args[@]}")
}

# core recipe, run from the caller's directory
_core() {
    (cd "${ARGC_PWD:-$PWD}" && argc --argc-run "$CORE" "$@")
}

_choice_plugin() {
    local d
    for d in "$PLUGINS"/*/.claude-plugin; do basename "$(dirname "$d")"; done
}

eval "$(argc --argc-eval "$0" "$@")"

---
name: argc
description: Use the skogai command runner (`argc`, skogai-runner's scripts/runner.sh) to hand typed work to other agents, run workorders, and improve the runner or a plugin. Use when delegating a bounded question or an edit, when a recipe is missing, or when asked to extend Argcfile.sh.
allowed-tools: Bash(argc --argc-run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/runner.sh *)
---

# argc

the runner is `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/runner.sh`, run from any directory:

```
argc --argc-run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/runner.sh <cmd>
```

file arguments are relative to the current directory; workorders, journal and logs live in `.skogai/` at the root of the current git repo (the current directory outside one). a repo can forward recipes from its own `Argcfile.sh`, then `argc <cmd>` works from anywhere in it; the recipes below are written that way. when the main runner is installed (`scripts/main.sh`, `~/Argcfile.sh`), `argc runner <cmd>` works anywhere under `~` without a repo `Argcfile.sh`; `argc ls` lists what is registered. `argc <cmd> --help` is the source of truth; this skill only says how to use them.

## the contract

the agent call behind `send` is one function:

```
send :: (prompt, [file], schema) -> json
```

- files are inlined, the worker gets no tools unless `--tools` says so.
- `--schema` names a file in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/schemas/` or a path. stdout is the json object; envelopes are logged to `.skogai/logs/argc/`.
- exit `0` ok or empty patch, `1` agent error or a patch printed but not applied (like `skogai plan`), `2` usage.

## recipes

| recipe | use |
|---|---|
| `argc send -p <q> -f <file>... -s answer` | one bounded question, short checkable answer |
| `argc send -s check -f <file>...` | findings as `{path, line, rule, severity, message}` |
| `argc improve <request> [-f file]... [--apply]` | whole-file edits from a worker, patch derived by `diff -u`. prints the patch unless `--apply` |
| `argc wo new <name> -s <schema> -f <file>...` | write `.skogai/workorders/<name>.md` |
| `argc wo run <name>` | run it, result in `<name>.result.json` |
| `argc journal prompts [file] [--last N] [--md]` | only the user's input from a session journal, one json row per turn |
| `argc journal harvest [file] [--last N] [--turns N]` | workers pick decisions, docs, todos, learnings out of a journal (schema `harvest`) |
| `argc check` | argc parse, shellcheck, schemas, this plugin |

## workorders

one bounded question per workorder. inputs are listed as files, never "go look around". output is a schema, so the result is checkable without reading prose.

```markdown
---
type: workorder
title: <name>
schema: answer
tools: ""
files:
  - path/to/input.md
---

<one bounded question>
```

## extending the runner

a recipe is a bash function with `# @cmd` above it; `foo::bar` is `argc foo bar`. flags and options become `$argc_<name>`. spec: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/specification.md`, the rest of `docs/` covers variables, completions, help format and macros.

recipes that every repo can use go in `scripts/runner.sh`; recipes for one repo go in that repo's `Argcfile.sh`. don't name the core `Argcfile.sh`: argc then runs it from its own directory instead of the caller's.

- pure by default. a recipe that writes takes `--apply`, and without it prints what it would do.
- a missing recipe is a gap: add it, or run `argc improve "<what it should do>"` and review the patch.
- keep a new schema small, `additionalProperties: false`, every field required.
- run `argc check` after a change.

from a skogai session, 2026-10-18 (skogai branch `bridge-cse_013WWYqpWeqHxJuZ6CaqYtLf`, `9212a5c` added it, `94e47d2` moved it here).

## intent

skogix's words: "you will be the one writing context, your intentions and will be the one managing yourself". this is the first iteration of that: your own command runner, the same commands everywhere, for handing strictly typed work to other agents. start by making it self-improving, so agents do the heavy lifting.

## what it is

- `scripts/runner.sh`: the core recipes, all built on `send :: (prompt, [file], schema) -> json` (`claude -p --json-schema`, read `.structured_output`).
- skill `argc` (how to use and extend the runner), schemas in `schemas/`, the argc docs in `docs/`.

send :: (prompt, [file], schema) -> json
```

| `argc marketplace json` | regenerate `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
| `argc marketplace evals <name>` | run a plugin's evals |
| `argc marketplace improve <name> <request> [--apply]` | `argc runner improve` over every file of a plugin |

one bounded question per workorder. inputs are listed as files, never "go look around". output is a schema, so the result is checkable without reading prose.

```markdown
---
type: workorder
title: <name>
schema: answer
tools: ""
files:
  - path/to/input.md
---

<one bounded question>
```

a recipe is a bash function with `# @cmd` above it; `foo::bar` is `argc <name> foo bar`. flags and options become `$argc_<name>`. spec: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/specification.md`, the rest of `docs/` covers variables, completions, help format and macros.

- don't name a script `Argcfile.sh`: argc then runs it from its own directory instead of the caller's.

- pure by default. a recipe that writes takes `--apply`, and without it prints what it would do.
- a missing recipe is a gap: add it, or run `argc runner improve "<what it should do>" -f <script>` and review the patch.
- keep a new schema small, `additionalProperties: false`, every field required.
- run `argc runner check` after a change, and `argc sync` after adding or renaming a recipe's top-level command.

# argc

the runner is `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/runner.sh`, run from any directory:

```
argc --argc-run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/runner.sh <cmd>
```

file arguments are relative to the current directory; workorders, journal and logs live in `.skogai/` at the root of the current git repo (the current directory outside one). a repo can forward recipes from its own `Argcfile.sh`, then `argc <cmd>` works from anywhere in it; the recipes below are written that way. when the main runner is installed (`scripts/main.sh`, `~/Argcfile.sh`), `argc runner <cmd>` works anywhere under `~` without a repo `Argcfile.sh`; `argc ls` lists what is registered. `argc <cmd> --help` is the source of truth; this skill only says how to use them.

## the contract

the agent call behind `send` is one function:

```
send :: (prompt, [file], schema) -> json
```

- files are inlined, the worker gets no tools unless `--tools` says so.
- `--schema` names a file in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/schemas/` or a path. stdout is the json object; envelopes are logged to `.skogai/logs/argc/`.
- exit `0` ok or empty patch, `1` agent error or a patch printed but not applied (like `skogai plan`), `2` usage.

## recipes

| recipe | use |
|---|---|
| `argc send -p <q> -f <file>... -s answer` | one bounded question, short checkable answer |
| `argc send -s check -f <file>...` | findings as `{path, line, rule, severity, message}` |
| `argc improve <request> [-f file]... [--apply]` | whole-file edits from a worker, patch derived by `diff -u`. prints the patch unless `--apply` |
| `argc wo new <name> -s <schema> -f <file>...` | write `.skogai/workorders/<name>.md` |
| `argc wo run <name>` | run it, result in `<name>.result.json` |
| `argc journal prompts [file] [--last N] [--md]` | only the user's input from a session journal, one json row per turn |
| `argc journal harvest [file] [--last N] [--turns N]` | workers pick decisions, docs, todos, learnings out of a journal (schema `harvest`) |
| `argc check` | argc parse, shellcheck, schemas, this plugin |

## workorders

one bounded question per workorder. inputs are listed as files, never "go look around". output is a schema, so the result is checkable without reading prose.

```markdown
---
type: workorder
title: <name>
schema: answer
tools: ""
files:
  - path/to/input.md
---

<one bounded question>
```

## extending the runner

a recipe is a bash function with `# @cmd` above it; `foo::bar` is `argc foo bar`. flags and options become `$argc_<name>`. spec: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/specification.md`, the rest of `docs/` covers variables, completions, help format and macros.

recipes that every repo can use go in `scripts/runner.sh`; recipes for one repo go in that repo's `Argcfile.sh`. don't name the core `Argcfile.sh`: argc then runs it from its own directory instead of the caller's.

- pure by default. a recipe that writes takes `--apply`, and without it prints what it would do.
- a missing recipe is a gap: add it, or run `argc improve "<what it should do>"` and review the patch.
- keep a new schema small, `additionalProperties: false`, every field required.
- run `argc check` after a change.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Claude Code plugin marketplace (`skogai-marketplace`). No build or test suite. `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` is generated by `scripts/generate-marketplace-json.sh` from `.claude-plugin/marketplace-header.json` (top-level fields), `plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/external-repos.json` (plugin source objects); never hand-edit it. `scripts/generate-marketplace-json.sh --check` fails if it drifted; the `marketplace` GitHub workflow and `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit` (`git config core.hooksPath scripts/git-hooks`) run it.

## Layout

- Local plugins live under `plugins/` and are listed with a `./plugins/<name>` source. No `metadata.pluginRoot` and no bare names: claude.ai organization sync rejects them. External plugins (no submodules) are listed in `.claude-plugin/external-repos.json`. An external repo without `plugin.json` gets its name and description from the `"./"` entry in its own `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, plus `"strict": false`, which organization sync requires for an inline manifest.
- Marketplace entries carry only `name`, `source`, `description` (and `strict` in that one case); `name` is kebab-case and matches the directory. Versions go in each plugin's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, not the marketplace entry.
- `docs/` is a synced snapshot of the Claude Code docs (date in `docs/synced-at.txt`). Treat it as the read-only reference for plugin/hook/marketplace APIs; never edit it.
- `CONVENTIONS.md` documents this repo's conventions and how the generator works.

## Validating

- `claude plugin validate plugins/<name>` — run after changing a plugin or its marketplace entry.
- `claude -p "reply with just OK" --plugin-dir plugins/<name>` — headless load check.
- `plugins/skogai-core/LEARNINGS.md` lists function-hook validator rules (string-literal event names, function-literal hooks, `$.noun.method()` only; one throwing hook stops the whole module loading). Read it before writing TypeScript hook modules.

## Git

Commit directly to `master`; short messages are fine.

## RULES

# APM – Agent Package Manager

**An open-source, community-driven dependency manager for AI agents.**

Think `package.json`, `requirements.txt`, or `Cargo.toml` — but for AI agent configuration.

GitHub Copilot | Claude Code | Grok Build | Cursor | OpenCode | Codex | Gemini | Windsurf | Kiro

**[Documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/)** · **[Quick Start](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/quickstart/)** · **[CLI Reference](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/)** · **[Roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/microsoft/projects/2304/views/5)**

---

> **Portable by manifest. Secure by default. Governed by policy.**
> One file describes every agent's context; one command reproduces it everywhere; one policy controls what an org will allow.

## Why APM

AI coding agents need context to be useful — standards, prompts, skills, plugins — but today every developer sets this up manually. Nothing is portable nor reproducible. There's no manifest for it.

**APM fixes this.** Declare your project's agentic dependencies once in `apm.yml`, and every developer who clones your repo gets a fully configured agent setup in seconds — with transitive dependency resolution, just like npm or pip. It's also the first tool that lets you **author plugins** with a real dependency manager and export standard `plugin.json` packages.

```yaml
# apm.yml — ships with your project
name: your-project
version: 1.0.0
targets:
  - copilot # choose the harness(es) this project supports
dependencies:
  apm:
    # Skills from any repository
    - anthropics/skills/skills/frontend-design
    # Plugins
    - github/awesome-copilot/plugins/context-engineering
    # Specific agent primitives from any repository
    - github/awesome-copilot/agents/api-architect.agent.md
    # A full APM package with instructions, skills, prompts, hooks...
    - microsoft/apm-sample-package#v1.0.0
  mcp:
    # MCP servers -- installed into every selected target
    - name: io.github.github/github-mcp-server
      transport: http   # MCP transport name, not URL scheme -- connects over HTTPS
```

```bash
git clone <org/repo> && cd <repo>
apm install    # every agent is configured
```

**Coming from `npx skills add`?** Drop-in:

```bash
apm install vercel-labs/agent-skills                            # whole bundle, like npx skills add
apm install vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill deploy-to-vercel   # one skill, persisted to apm.yml
```

Same install gesture. You also get a [manifest, lockfile, and reproducibility](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/package-types/#skill-collection-skillsnameskillmd).

**Zero-config Copilot:**

Partly. apm is a good fit for managing the repo's own dev setup, but not yet for generating `marketplace.json`.

**Where apm can take over:**
- apm's marketplace feature does the same job as `scripts/generate-marketplace-json.sh`. You'd declare the entries in a `marketplace:` block in `apm.yml`, and `apm pack` writes `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. It handles both kinds of entry you have: local `./plugins/<name>` paths, and remote `url` / `git-subdir` sources like codex, loadout and open-knowledge.
- It also adds things the script lacks: version ranges resolved against git tags, `apm marketplace check` and `outdated`, and an optional Codex marketplace file.

**What blocks replacing the generator now:**
- **`strict: false`:** I found no code in apm's marketplace builder that writes it. Organization sync needs it on `open-knowledge-plugin`.
- **`renames`:** not supported either, so the entries that clear out `forge`, `verity` and `jetbrains-router` would be lost.
- **Plugin layout:** apm expects each plugin's content under `.apm/<type>/`. Your plugins use the native Claude layout, and skogai-core ships TypeScript hook modules.

**One risk in the working tree:** the untracked `apm.yml` still contains the `apm marketplace init` placeholder block (`acme-org`, `example-package`). Running `apm pack` now would overwrite the real `marketplace.json` with that placeholder, and the pre-commit `--check` would then fail.

**Where it fits today:** declaring this repo's MCP servers, skills and so on, which is what your `apm install` already did. The netdata `mcp-server` it added fails to connect in this session with a 401, so it needs a valid token or should be removed.

I posted the decision as Q2 with four options: consumer only, replace generator, both outputs, or drop apm here. I recommended consumer only: keep the generator as the source of truth and remove the placeholder `marketplace:` block. Replacing the generator would mean adding `strict` and `renames` support to apm first.

name: skogai-marketplace
version: 1.0.0
description: skogai-marketplace
author: Emil Skogsund
# Which agent platforms to deploy to.
# Resolution order: --target flag > this field > auto-detect from filesystem.
# Accepted values: agent-skills, antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, grok-bot, grok-build, hermes, kiro, opencode, vscode, windsurf
targets:
- claude
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp: []
includes: auto
scripts: {}
marketplace:
  owner:
    name: skogix
    url: https://github.com/skogai

  # Default tag pattern used to resolve version ranges for each package.
  build:
    tagPattern: "v{version}"

  # Output targets (map form). 'claude' is enabled by default;
  # uncomment 'codex' below to publish the Codex artifact too.
  # Each output writes to its profile default path; add 'path:'
  # under a key to override.
  outputs:
    claude:
      path: build/apm-marketplace.json
    # codex: {}
    #
    # Note: enabling codex requires every package below to declare
    # 'category:' (e.g. category: Productivity).

  # CI tip: build one or all formats with a machine-readable manifest:
  #   apm pack --marketplace=claude,codex --json | jq -r '.marketplace.outputs[].path'

  packages:
  - name: skogai-core
    source: ./plugins/skogai-core
    version: 0.8.0
  - name: skogai-council
    source: ./plugins/skogai-council
    version: 2026.10.11
  - name: skogai-runner
    source: ./plugins/skogai-runner
    version: 0.9.1
  - name: loadout
    source: https://github.com/skogai2/loadout
    ref: 6695e2fe3a87ff81eae22c7ab5435f3c6e8ccebd
  - name: open-knowledge-plugin
    source: https://github.com/skogai2/open-knowledge-plugin
    ref: 5329c530e154b1109a78da040aa084c5479790bc
  - name: codex
    source: openai/codex-plugin-cc
    ref: db52e28f4d9ded852ab3942cea316258ae4ef346
    subdir: plugins/codex

cd /home/skogix/.local/src/marketplace; python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import json,re
d={p["name"]:p["description"] for p in json.load(open(".claude-plugin/marketplace.json"))["plugins"]}
out=[]
for line in open("apm.yml"):
    if line.startswith("dependencies:") or line.startswith("  apm: []") or line.startswith("  mcp: []"): continue
    out.append(line)
    m=re.match(r"  - name: (\S+)",line)
    if m: out.append("    description: "+json.dumps(d[m.group(1)])+"\n")
open("apm.yml","w").write("".join(out))
EOF
apm pack 2>&1 | grep -v "^\[i\]"; ls build .claude-plugin; diff <(jq -S '.plugins|sort_by(.name)|map({name,description})' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json) <(jq -S '.plugins|sort_by(.name)|map({name,description})' build/apm-marketplace.json) && echo descriptions match

title: Installing from marketplaces
description: Six ways consumers install APM-published plugins -- through APM, VS Code, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Claude Code, and Codex -- and the auth and cache layout of each.
sidebar:
  order: 2
---

A marketplace publisher (see
[Publish to a marketplace](../../producer/publish-to-a-marketplace/))
ships one `marketplace.json` that every major agent runtime can read.
This page covers the install side: which command each runtime
exposes, what authentication it needs, and where files land on disk.

The recommended path is `apm install`. It is the only path that gives
you a committed `apm.lock.yaml`, content-hash pinning, transitive
resolution, the pre-install security scan, and `apm audit --ci`
drift detection. Use a native command when you cannot install APM,
or when the runtime owns the install surface (VS Code Copilot Chat).

## Install patterns

| Runtime                         | Install command                                                         | Auth                                | Cache layout                                                                 |
|---------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| APM (recommended)               | `apm marketplace add <owner>/<repo>` then `apm install <pkg>@<marketplace>` | HTTPS: host token or git credential helper. SSH: local key or agent. | `apm_modules/` in the project; `~/.apm/cache/` for fetched refs.             |
| VS Code (GitHub Copilot Chat)   | Plugin marketplace UI; or `code --install-extension` for the marketplace itself. | VS Code GitHub sign-in.             | Per-user extension store managed by VS Code. APM artifacts stream from the marketplace at activation. |
| Cursor                          | Settings -> Plugins -> add marketplace URL.                             | Cursor account.                     | `~/.cursor/extensions/` per-user.                                            |
| GitHub Copilot CLI              | `gh copilot marketplace add <owner>/<repo>` then `gh copilot plugin install <pkg>`. | `gh auth login`.                    | `~/.config/gh/copilot/` per-user.                                            |
| Claude Code                     | `/plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>` then `/plugin install <pkg>`.  | Anthropic sign-in.                  | `~/.claude/plugins/` per-user; `.claude/` in-project when wired.             |
| OpenAI Codex CLI 0.163.0        | `codex plugin marketplace add ...` then `codex plugin add <pkg>@<marketplace>`. | Native activation and authentication remain with Codex. | User cache managed by Codex; not an APM project registration. |

Native commands above read whichever artifact the runtime expects.
Most read `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Anthropic-compatible
schema); Codex reads `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. Producers
who enable both outputs reach every runtime from one repo.

## Codex compatibility bundles through APM

APM recognizes a compatibility-only `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` without
reducing its bundle to loose skills. This route is qualified for **Codex CLI
0.163.0 on `PATH`, user scope only**:

```sh
apm install -g <package> --target codex
apm install -g --frozen --target codex
apm uninstall -g <package>
```

Native qualification was measured on **macOS arm64 only**. Other platforms
are not qualified by that evidence; APM checks the version and scope, not the OS.

Approve the package's executable types in `allowExecutables` first. APM scans
and transfers the complete bundle, including sibling assets and referenced MCP
resources, then uses Codex's public app-server configuration and marketplace
operations. New registrations are **disabled**. Reinstall, update, and repair
preserve existing activation, explicit disables, MCP policy, and unrelated
settings. APM never runs plugin/MCP code or grants native trust or authentication.

The initial contract supports MCP server objects and package-relative JSON
files containing `mcpServers`. At least one native-discoverable `SKILL.md` must
provide an unambiguous installed path so APM can verify the complete native
copy. Symlinks, skill subsets, unsupported MCP shapes, other Codex versions,
and project-scope registration fail explicitly rather than silently dropping
resources or claiming native loading. This is a content-discovery contract,
not evidence that an MCP process can start or authenticate.

APM keeps its transport snapshots and ownership journal in
`$APM_HOME/.codex-native/` (normally `~/.apm/.codex-native/`), outside disposable
`apm_modules/`. Missing or corrupt native copies are restored through a
selected native marketplace refresh with a new transport generation. Publisher
bytes, publisher version, and original dependency pins remain unchanged;
a healthy reinstall does not create a new generation. Keep the ownership
journal: APM refuses to adopt a matching native registration without it.
Native fingerprints include publisher `__pycache__` assets and executable
bits; existing APM lockfile hashes are unchanged. The validated ownership
journal also identifies native bundles during a cold-cache frozen restore
alongside unrelated loose MCP declarations. A missing or `0.0.0` native
version does not authorize rewriting publisher `apm.yml` metadata.
Running `apm audit --ci` from the APM user directory checks the cached source
bundle without starting Codex. Native-copy verification happens during install.
The journal binds each remote bundle's native fingerprint to its original Git
